title: Pass GitHub credentials to the steward so gh can read CI and PRs
summary: The steward's `gh` fails because agents start from an empty environment and `athena.toml` `[agents] env_pass_if_set` lists no GitHub variable (`GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`). I will add the GitHub variables to that list, record the decision, and update the steward docs. The audience is the steward and the owner who reads its blind-spot report.

defaults_applied.how: The fix targets the allow-list that strips the credential, not a one-off workaround.
The allow-list in athena.toml is the mechanism, and a test pins that the GitHub variables pass only when set.
No token value is written anywhere; only variable names are.
Add a unit test for env::build with GH_TOKEN set and unset; cargo test and clippy stay clean.
The decision record cites env.rs and athena.toml as its sources.
One config line, one decision, one doc sentence and one test.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Root cause, read from crates/athena-agent/src/env.rs and athena.toml: agents start with an empty environment and only HOME and PATH are always passed. Neither GH_TOKEN nor GITHUB_TOKEN is on the list, so gh cannot authenticate unless a gh config under HOME exists.
docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md already says the steward is only as able to read GitHub as env_pass_if_set allows, so the allow-list is the intended place for the fix.
The change adds GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_HOST and GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN, each passed only when set. I did not add GH_CONFIG_DIR.

I cannot confirm that the owner's shell has a token set. If it does not, the change alone will not make gh readable. The docs will then say the owner must export a read-only token before running Athena.
Only the steward's gh reads are allowed by policy.rs, and the token reaches every agent role's environment. The decision record will state that tradeoff and recommend a read-only token.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena.toml `[agents] env_pass_if_set` includes GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN, and `env_pass` is unchanged. The comment above the list mentions GitHub.
Run `cargo test -p athena-agent`. A new env.rs test shows that GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN appear in the built environment when the lookup supplies them, and are absent when unset or empty.

docs/decisions.md has a new decision, in the same format as D53, that explains why gh failed (an empty agent environment with no GitHub variable). It names the alternatives (a gh config under HOME; no access with a recorded blind spot) and the tradeoff of a token in the agent environment.
docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md's GitHub bullet names the variables passed and tells the owner to export a read-only token. The steward docs state that without it the `github` blind spot is reported.
Run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy`. Both pass, including any test that parses athena.toml.

out_of_scope: Creating, storing or printing any token or credential
Running `gh auth login` or changing the owner's machine or shell setup
Loosening the gh read-only command policy in crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs
Changing the model, budget or timeout of the steward
